title: Facial classification Using Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning
authors: Roshan Babu Bandlapalli, Srinivas V Katakam, Jitendra Chougala, Ravi Kumar Kappagantu, Jayasri Dontabhaktuni
abstract: Hybrid quantum methods have received limited study for resource-constrained facial biometrics. We present a hybrid quantum-classical facial recognition pipeline designed to run on standard computing hardware. Images undergo gamma correction, contrast enhancement, and principal component analysis before their features are encoded into an eight-qubit variational quantum classifier. Classical image matching then performs recognition. In experiments with 50,000 images, comprising 25,000 faces from CelebA and 25,000 non-face images from CIFAR-10, the method outperformed the reported CPU-trained FaceNet baseline in accuracy and training efficiency. The pipeline was also evaluated on GPU and quantum hardware. In an attendance monitoring deployment at Mahindra University in collaboration with Lloyds Technology Centre, CPU inference took 0.2 to 0.5 seconds per person, and the system remained robust to the use of spectacles. These findings support the feasibility of deploying hybrid quantum methods for facial recognition on existing CPU hardware.
summary: This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline for facial recognition designed to run on standard CPUs. It combines classical image enhancement and dimensionality reduction with an 8-qubit Variational Quantum Classifier. The method successfully demonstrated high accuracy and fast inference times, proving the feasibility of deploying quantum-enhanced biometrics on existing hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational overhead of classical deep learning for facial biometrics, proposing a hybrid quantum-classical approach for resource-constrained environments.
main_result: The hybrid pipeline achieved high accuracy (up to 98%) and demonstrated practical viability, outperforming classical baselines on CPU hardware with fast inference times.
method: It uses classical preprocessing (PCA, enhancement) to reduce features, which are then encoded into an 8-qubit Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) for final classification.
model_or_system: The core model is a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline featuring an 8-qubit VQC built with parameterized entangling circuits. The classical side involves image processing steps like gamma correction and PCA.
key_observables: Accuracy (up to 98%), inference time (0.2 to 0.5 seconds per person), and comparison against classical baselines like FaceNet.
important_parameters: The number of qubits (8), the number of VQC layers (3), and the dimensionality reduction factor (PCA to 8 components).
main_assumptions: The classical preprocessing steps (e.g., Haar cascade) are sufficient for controlled settings, and the hybrid approach balances quantum expressivity with NISQ hardware constraints.

paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of identifying the limitations of classical methods, proposing the hybrid quantum-classical architecture, detailing the specific components (preprocessing, encoding, VQC ansatz), and validating the system through extensive experiments on various hardware platforms.
why_interesting: The work directly applies quantum machine learning techniques (VQC) to a practical, real-world problem (biometrics), providing concrete performance metrics and feasibility studies relevant to near-term quantum hardware deployment.

Stage 1 performs classical preprocessing such as Haar cascade detection, ROI extrac- tion, gamma correction, CLAHE enhancement, and PCA dimensionality reduction. Stage 2 applies quantum processing via angle embedding, multi-layer strong entanglement, and mea- surement for face/non-face classification, followed by database matching for authentication.

Figure 2: Single layer of Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) anstaz for facial detection im- plemented on 8-qubit register (one of three variational layers illustrated). The circuit comprises three principal components: (i) Angle embedding, (ii) Strongly entangling layers, fol- lowed by nearest-neighbor circular CNOT entanglement to promote feature correlation across the register; and (iii) Measurement stage, where Pauli-Z expectation values are extracted from selected qubits for binary classification.
